title: JSON Preview interpolates column names without escaping, producing invalid JSON for names containing quotes/backslashes/newlines
description: The "JSON Preview" block builds a JSON-looking string by raw template-interpolating each selected field name: `fields.map((f) => `  "${f}": ...`).join(",\n")`. Field names are upstream Polars column names, which can legitimately contain double-quotes, backslashes, or newlines (Polars permits arbitrary column-name strings). For such a column the rendered preview is not valid JSON (e.g. a column named `a"b` renders as `  "a"b": ...`), so the panel labelled 'JSON Preview' would misrepresent the actual response shape. The correct idiom is to serialize the key via `JSON.stringify(f)` (which yields a properly-escaped, quoted key) instead of wrapping in literal quotes. Impact is display-only — the string lives inside a `<pre>` and is never parsed or sent over the wire — so there is no runtime/security consequence, only a misleading preview for unusual column names.
